pr_title: tracing: fix inconsistent lock ordering when notifying event listeners
pr_body:
This change fixes an inconsistent lock ordering that was caught in #81361.
As per the lock ordering convention between a parent, and a child span
we now notify the parent of StructuredEvents recorded by the child outside
of the child span's lock.

Additionally, we now notify the event listeners without holding the span's mutex.
This is to protect against deadlocks if the `Notify` method were to call methods
on the tracing span which acquire the span's mutex. One can imagine `Notify` calling
`SetLazyTag` on the same tracing span as the one that has the event
listener.

Fixes: #81361

Release note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/81379)

> Let's add a test that would have deadlocked before?

`TestEventListener`, when run under deadlock, shook this potential deadlock out. Were you thinking of something more in addition to that? - https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/81361

> I don't know if I buy the SetLazyTag usecase,

I'm playing around with something in https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/81270 that led to this pattern but we can have that conversation on that PR.

> That makes sense, but then why is eventListeners under s.mu?

~~We can have multiple child span's recording structured events and calling `parent.NotifyEventListeners` in turn so I think we do need the mutex to prevent concurrent reads?~~

~~edit: I'm not sure about this anymore, maybe concurrent readers of a slice never being written too is okay? Still looking for a an authoritative google result.~~

Moving it out of the mutex, I've been told reads are safe if all writes occur before the goroutines that read.

> would it be a problem for the event listeners to be notified of an event after the span is finished

 No, atleast as of now I don't think it would be a problem.

review_comments: @andreimatei should we be taking a reference to the parent here instead? The situation I'm trying to wrap my head around is the parent Finish() racing with the call to `parent.notifyEventListeners` below.

Additionally, I don't think we should be holding on to `s.mu` mutex while calling `Notify` in the loop below. `Notify` could in turn be calling a method on the tracing span egs: `SetLazyTag` and that would cause a deadlock. I'm thinking of creating a copy of the `s.mu.eventListeners` slice while holding the mutex, and then operating on it outside of the span's mutex. 

Initially, I thought we could just operate on `s.mu.eventListeners` outside s.mu since we don't expect the slice to change given the only API to add event listeners is on creation. We could however race with the span being finished.
